topics.label: Course introduction and overview of inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes students and frames the lecture's focus on integrating previously introduced immune components into complete inflammatory reactions.

topics.label: Innate immune recognition through PAMPs, DAMPs, and pattern recognition receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how innate sentinel cells detect microbial products and cellular damage through diverse pattern recognition receptors and downstream signaling structures.

topics.label: Inflammatory cascade execution, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic consequences
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the physiological mechanisms of the active inflammatory response, from sentinel activation and leukocyte extravasation to adaptive immune priming and septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic containment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how acute inflammation is brought to an end, how damaged tissue is repaired, and how persistent stimuli lead to chronic inflammation and granuloma formation.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview of complement
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and announces the subject of the next lecture.
